items.title: How Does a CDN Handle Content Replication
items.summary: A CDN handles content replication by proactively sending content to edge nodes, using two primary approaches: push-based replication and content-addressed storage. Most modern CDNs use a hybrid of both. They ensure consistency by placing copies of content geographically closer to users, but determine what to replicate, where to place it, and when to update.
